profile_text.body:
NVIDIA Research is the research arm of NVIDIA, based in Santa Clara, California, and described in the company's own materials as a for-profit research lab. On its site the group says it is passionate about developing technology and finding the breakthroughs that bring positive change to the world, and it points visitors to work in generative AI, graphics, and related areas.

The site highlights an AI Playground where users can try demos from its research teams, and a set of open-source resources meant to simplify programming tasks for AI researchers: NVIDIA Sionna, Kaolin, Kaolin Wisp, Imaginaire, and CUDA-X. NVIDIA AI Foundation Models are presented as an easy-to-use interface for trying curated and optimized AI models directly from a browser, running on the NVIDIA accelerated computing stack. Kaolin is described as a PyTorch library that accelerates 3D deep learning research through differentiable 3D modules and a curated model zoo of 3D deep learning architectures. CUDA is described as a parallel computing platform and programming model developed by NVIDIA for general computing on GPUs, with CUDA-X as a collection of libraries for AI and high-performance computing built on top of it.

The held record lists no tracked products, no MCP servers, and no individual cases for the company. It does carry a litigation exposure count of 281 for California.
